item.title: An Artist Inspired by Men Behaving Badly
item.description: In a new show at David Kordansky Gallery, the Iranian American painter Tala Madani plumbs the lives of her characters with absurd humor and a strange tenderness.
item.dc:creator: Aruna D’Souza
item.media:credit: Maiwenn Raoult for The New York Times
item.media:description: The artist Tala Madani with “Disco-ball Break Out,” 2026. She paints the disco as a place where people indulge their impulses, sometimes with disastrous effects.

item.title: Bayeux Tapestry Exhibition Opens at British Museum
item.description: On Thursday, the British Museum opened its blockbuster Bayeux Tapestry exhibition, its most eagerly anticipated show in decades.
item.dc:creator: Alex Marshall

item.title: Where to See the World’s Bayeux Tapestry Replicas
item.description: There are full-size replicas in a U.S. sports arena, an abbey in Denmark and a home in rural New Zealand. There’s even a more modest version for those who don’t like the original’s nudity.
item.dc:creator: Alex Marshall

item.title: Can the 9/11 Museum Tell Its Story for Another 25 Years?
item.description: As the anniversary of the terrorist attacks approaches, the museum is gradually adding new displays and confronting its financial future.
item.dc:creator: Zachary Small
item.media:credit: Timothy O'Connell for The New York Times
item.media:description: The 9/11 Memorial & Museum is adding new displays, including a temporary exhibition that focuses on how Americans turned grief into action.

item.title: The Young Women at the Heart of American Landscape Art
item.description: Once dismissed as exercises in dainty femininity, the handiwork of schoolgirls is now celebrated for anticipating the art of the Hudson River School and beyond.
item.dc:creator: Celia McGee

item.title: Smithsonian’s Secretary to Resign as Trump Tries to Rule the Institution
item.description: In the face of escalating White House attacks about how museums present American history, Lonnie G. Bunch III has announced his decision to depart.
item.dc:creator: Robin Pogrebin and Graham Bowley
item.category: National Museum of African American History and Culture
item.media:description: Lonnie G. Bunch III, the secretary of the Smithsonian, has tried to navigate increasing pressure from the White House while defending the institution’s autonomy.

item.title: Art’s New Season: Retrospectives and Resistance
item.description: Holland Cotter’s highlights include a panoptic view of Roy Lichtenstein, storytelling surprises of the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art, and activism from Colombia to South Asia to New York.
item.dc:creator: Holland Cotter

item.title: 25 Global Art Openings Worth Making an Excursion For
item.description: Our critic Jason Farago awaits Brancusi at MoMA, a K-pop icon’s collection in San Francisco, Sofia Coppola at the Château de Versailles — and new art centers in New York.
item.dc:creator: Jason Farago
item.category: Guggenheim Abu Dhabi (United Arab Emirates, Museum)
Wallach, Miriam and Ira D, Art Gallery

item.title: Lonnie G. Bunch III, Departing Smithsonian Secretary, Faced ‘Mounting Pressure Campaign’
item.description: Under Lonnie G. Bunch III’s leadership, President Trump accused the Smithsonian of liberal, anti-American bias. Supporters say he was dedicated to nonpartisan scholarship.
item.dc:creator: Zachary Small, Graham Bowley and Robin Pogrebin
item.category: National Museum of African American History and Culture
item.media:description: Lonnie G. Bunch III announced on Tuesday that he would step down as the secretary of the Smithsonian Institution.

item.title: Ousted Kennedy Center Chairman Buys Dismantled ‘Blue’ Sculpture
item.description: David Rubenstein purchased the sculpture, which was removed from the center last week, from the artist’s foundation. He will display it at the National Gallery of Art.
item.dc:creator: Julia Jacobs
item.category: Kennedy, John F, Center for the Performing Arts
item.media:credit: The Joel Shapiro and Ellen Phelan Foundation/Artists Rights Society (ARS), New York; Photograph by Salwan Georges for The New York Times
item.media:description: “Blue,” by the artist Joel Shapiro, sat on the Kennedy Center’s grounds from 2019 until last week.

item.title: There Is Still a Void at Ground Zero. Here’s How We Fill It.
item.description: At 25 years, the World Trade Center is an undeniable feat of urban redevelopment. Now we can make it a real neighborhood.
item.dc:creator: Michael Kimmelman and George Etheredge
item.category: Perelman, Ronald O, Performing Arts Center
St Nicholas National Shrine at the World Trade Center (Manhattan, NY)

item.title: What to Do With Europe’s ‘Zombie Churches’? These Artists Have Some Ideas.
item.description: As the continent’s ties to Christianity fade, churches are being abandoned. But some see a chance to transform them into communal spaces like care centers or venues for the arts.
item.dc:creator: Nina Siegal

item.title: Krasner & Pollock, Lichtenstein and RM Make Art’s New Season Pop This Fall
item.description: Look for a wide-ranging survey of Black abstraction at MoMA PS1, Taryn Simon’s photographic explorations in the Guggenheim Museum rotunda, Eric Carle’s colorful collages and much more.
item.dc:creator: Will Heinrich

item.title: What Is ‘Narrative Art’? The Lucas Museum Finally Shows Us Its Vision.
item.description: After several delays, George Lucas’s legacy project is finally ready to open. There’s less “Star Wars” than you might expect.
item.dc:creator: Matt Stevens, Robin Pogrebin and Adam Amengual
item.media:description: The Lucas Museum of Narrative Art intends to present the images and objects that make stories come alive.

item.title: Unstitching the 1,000-Year-Old Story of the Bayeux Tapestry
item.description: The medieval masterpiece has traveled from France to England for a once-in-a-lifetime show. It is not what our critic Jason Farago expected.
item.dc:creator: Jason Farago

item.title: At the New York Studio School, a Renovation Provides a History Lesson
item.description: A recent renovation of the landmark New York Studio School turned up a hidden mural and other gems.
item.dc:creator: Jane Margolies
item.media:credit: Katherine Marks for The New York Times
item.media:description: The renovation work at the New York Studio School in Greenwich Village uncovered a mural featuring nearly floor-to-ceiling Doric columns by Robert E. Locher.

item.title: How to Do a Fall Reset, According to Artists, Chefs and Writers
item.description: We asked artists, designers, chefs and writers how they’re embracing the seasonal shift and preparing for upcoming projects.
item.dc:creator: Flora Stubbs

item.title: 8 Design Products Inspired by Nature
item.description: How product designers are inspired by fading flowers, the properties of ice and water and tree bark as a ready-made.
item.dc:creator: Diana Budds

item.title: A Unique Midcentury Home Gets a Subtle Restoration
item.description: In suburban Connecticut, a fashion executive and a designer updated one of Richard Neutra’s only remaining East Coast projects.
item.dc:creator: Jameson Montgomery and Daniel Paik

item.title: Tippet Rise: Where Music and Art Meet Postcard Mountain Views
item.description: Tippet Rise Art Center in Montana offers concerts in surroundings that make you feel as if you’re listening inside the land rather than around it.
item.dc:creator: David Allen and Will Warasila

item.title: Jean-François Leroy, Champion of Photography at Its Rawest, Dies at 69
item.description: His photojournalism festival, Visa Pour l’Image, brought to wide attention images of war and suffering. The French president called him “a great defender of reality.”
item.dc:creator: Adam Nossiter
item.media:credit: Stephane De Sakutin/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: Jean-François Leroy in 2017. Visa Pour l’Image, which he co-founded in 1989, has been a home for distinguished, daring work.

item.title: How Bedouine’s Family Heirlooms Inspired an Album
item.description: The musician Bedouine was reluctant to inherit dozens of heirlooms. Then, they inspired an album.
item.dc:creator: Julia Halperin

item.title: In San Francisco, the Artist Joset Medina’s Walls Have Boundary Issues
item.description: Joset Medina’s entire apartment is his canvas in the evolving project that he calls the “Unrestrained Garden.”
item.dc:creator: Stephen Treffinger and Matthew Millman
item.media:description: Joset Medina’s apartment walls are slathered in vines, branches and cacti representing his mother and grandmother’s gardens in Venezuela, his circuitous emigration to California and his travels with his husband.

item.title: A Japanese Polymath Transforms a Modernist Icon
item.description: Hiroshi Sugimoto’s redesign of the Hirshhorn Museum’s sculpture garden was a heavy lift that will finally see the light.
item.dc:creator: Sam Lubell and Rob Cardillo
item.media:description: Hiroshi Sugimoto, the man behind the redesign of the garden at the Hirshhorn Museum and Sculpture Garden. This was his second commission from the museum; he previously reworked the lobby.

item.title: Can Art Revitalize a Small Mountain Town in North Carolina?
item.description: In North Carolina’s Lost Provinces, residents see the arts as a pathway to sustainability and maintaining community.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Abrams
item.category: Lost Province Center for the Cultural Arts
item.media:credit: Mike Belleme for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Lansing School, tucked away in tiny Ashe County, N.C., fell into disarray. Now, some in the area are transforming it into a hub for the region’s lost arts.

item.title: Ambassador Who Removed Kehinde Wiley Work Described It as a Lesbian Picnic
item.description: Trump officials recently removed a painting from the U.S. Embassy in the Dominican Republic without explaining why. An interview by Ambassador Leah Campos shed some light.
item.dc:creator: Zachary Small
item.media:credit: Ian C. Bates for The New York Times

item.title: A Hotel Had the Perfect Chairs. How Do I Get Them at Home?
item.description: The story behind a pair of seats at New York’s Fifth Avenue Hotel.
item.dc:creator: Tom Delavan
